title: ISOLATION PUMP · ARMS & DELTS
vibe: GREEN · You asked for isolation — here's a pure hypertrophy day. No compound grinds, no ballistics, no treadmill: just direct arm, shoulder, chest and back work taken near failure with partials and drop sets. Legs got hammered Thursday, so today they rest while your sleeves do the work. Push it — the point today is to chase a real pump, not to move heavy iron.
why: You did the SINGLE-SIDE LEGS · REDLINE session Thursday (07-23) — heavy unilateral strength plus a single-leg redline — and your legs are still a touch sore two days out, so hammering them again would be junk work. You told me two things: push it, and give you MORE ISOLATION. Both point the same direction. Your log is almost all compound density, ballistics, carries and unilateral strength — direct isolation and hypertrophy-pump work is the single biggest gap in it (only your 07-17 6-12-25 finisher scratched it). So today is a dedicated bodybuilding day, upper-body only: it spares the sore legs, fills that gap, and is exactly what you asked for. You're GREEN (7h sleep, only mild leg DOMS), so this isn't a light day — you push every isolation move to near failure using the techniques the research lens surfaced: 21s and lengthened partials for constant tension, and drop-set burnouts to chase true fatigue. Your cardio today comes from the pump density itself — short rests and burnout rounds spike the heart rate without a single junk-impact mile (you've run enough; steady easy Zone 2 stays your open gap for a lighter day if you want an easy jog later, but it's optional). Wildcard = 21s curls: bottom-half, top-half, full-range — a bodybuilding isolation staple you've literally never done in this log.

blocks.title: MOBILITY WARM-UP
blocks.meta: ~6 min · Moves Method Day A (shoulders / spine / elbows / wrists) · prime the joints you're about to isolate
blocks.text: Upper-isolation day, so open the shoulders and bulletproof the elbows and wrists before you load them with high-rep curls, extensions and raises. OS resets: diaphragmatic breathing x5 · cross-crawls 10/side. Then Day A: arm circles 10 each way · shoulder dislocates (broomstick/towel) x10 · band or bodyweight scap wall-slides x10 · thoracic rotations 8/side (open the T-spine) · wrist rocks + wrist circles 15 each (elbow/wrist insurance for all the curl volume) · light 16 kg pump-up: 8 curls + 8 presses just to feed blood in. Get a light pump before the working sets — warm joints and pre-fed muscle = more reps near failure and less elbow cranking.

blocks.title: BLOCK 1 · ARM ISOLATION (antagonist superset)
blocks.meta: ~13 min · 16 kg (or 50 lb DB for triceps) · biceps + triceps back-to-back · RPE 8–9, near failure
blocks.format: ANTAGONIST SUPERSET · 4 rounds · A1 then A2 back-to-back · rest ~45s after each pair · final round = drop-set / partial burnout to failure
blocks.workRest: Curl and extension alternate with no rest between them (one pumps while the other recovers), then rest ~45s and go again. Strict elbows — the elbow does NOT drift; only the forearm moves. Pre-engage the muscle before each rep, squeeze hard at the top, and fight the weight down for 2–3 seconds. Rounds 1–3 are clean strict reps; on round 4 you take BOTH moves past failure with the burnout cue in each.

items.name: A1 · 21s Curl (WILDCARD)
items.detail: 16 kg by the horns, ~35 lb bilateral (or single-arm 21s each side if two-hand feels awkward) · 7 bottom-half reps (full stretch to mid) + 7 top-half reps (mid to peak squeeze) + 7 full-range = 21 total. Elbows pinned to your ribs, palms supinated, no shoulder swing. Round 4: after the 21, keep curling slow full reps until you can't — drop-set to true failure.

items.name: A2 · Overhead Triceps Extension
items.detail: 16 kg in both hands overhead (or 50 lb DB) · 12–15 reps · elbows tight and pointing at the ceiling, lower behind the head for a deep stretch, drive to a locked-out squeeze. Only the forearms move. Round 4: when full reps stop, keep pulsing bottom-third lengthened partials (deep stretch position) until failure.

blocks.text: Straight-up arm day. Supersetting biceps and triceps lets each recover while the other works, so you get more quality volume in less time and a huge pump — perfect for the 45-min cap. The 21s are your wildcard and your headline: seven bottom-half, seven top-half, seven full — the research today was explicit that partial ranges plus near-failure drop sets drive bicep growth better than chasing load, and strict elbow position is everything. Triceps get the same treatment: deep stretch, hard lockout, then lengthened partials to finish. Push these — clean reps for three rounds, then bury both on round four.

blocks.title: BLOCK 2 · DELT ISOLATION (3-way giant set)
blocks.meta: ~11 min · 16 kg · all three delt heads · RPE 8, partials to burn
blocks.format: GIANT SET · 3 rounds · B1 → B2 → B3 with no rest inside the round · rest ~60s between rounds
blocks.workRest: One bell, three delt heads, straight through — side, rear, front — then rest a minute and repeat. Shoulders love volume and constant tension, so lead with the elbow, control every descent, and when strict reps run out, keep pumping partials in the stretch. Lighten your grip and slow down if the elbows complain — this is a burn, not a grind.

items.name: B1 · Lateral Raise (lengthened partials)
items.detail: 16 kg single-arm, alternate arms · 10–12/side · lead with the elbow, raise to shoulder height, control the descent for 2s. When strict reps stop, keep pumping bottom-third partials (the lengthened position where the side delt works hardest) until it burns out. 16 kg is heavy for a lateral — a slight lean and partials are expected and correct here.

items.name: B2 · Bent-Over Rear-Delt Row-Raise
items.detail: 16 kg single-arm (or 50 lb DB) · 12–15/side · hinge to ~45°, high elbow, pull/raise out to the side and squeeze the rear delt at the top — no traps, no yank. The row bias lets you handle the 16 kg through a full range.

items.name: B3 · Front Raise / Press-Out
items.detail: 16 kg both hands · 10–12 · raise to eye level with straight-ish arms (or press slightly out and up), control down. Front-delt finisher to round out all three heads.

blocks.text: Capped delts are what make arms look built, and they never get direct work in your log — it's all presses and swings. So all three heads in one giant set: side (with lengthened partials, the highest-tension position), rear (row-biased so you can load it), and front. It'll burn fast and drive blood into the shoulder. The 16 kg is genuinely heavy for lateral raises — don't ego it into a full clean rep; partials in the stretch are the point and they grow the delt just as well.

blocks.title: BLOCK 3 · CHEST + BACK PUMP (superset + burnout)
blocks.meta: ~8 min · 16 kg + 50 lb DB · squeeze-tension isolation · this is your cardio — keep rests short
blocks.format: SUPERSET · 3 rounds · C1 + C2 back-to-back · rest ~40s · ROUND 3 = double burnout to failure
blocks.workRest: Short rests here on purpose — the pump density is your conditioning today, so keep moving and let your heart rate climb. Constant tension is the whole game: crush the bell the entire chest set, and keep the arms long on the pullover. Round 3 is the burnout — take both moves to failure, pause 10s, squeeze out 5 more of each.

items.name: C1 · KB Crush-Grip Squeeze Press
items.detail: 16 kg, standing or on the floor · 12–15 · crush the bell hard between both palms the ENTIRE set and press it out and up, squeezing your chest together at lockout. The crush keeps constant adduction tension on the pecs — that squeeze IS the exercise. Hold nothing back on the top squeeze.

items.name: C2 · Straight-Arm Pullover
items.detail: 50 lb DB (or 16 kg) lying on the floor · 12–15 · arms nearly straight, lower the weight overhead for a big lat + serratus stretch, then pull it back over your chest with the lats — don't bend the elbows. Feel the stretch, own the squeeze.

blocks.text: Chest and back get isolation-flavored work to finish the upper body: the crush-grip press hammers the pecs through pure squeeze tension (no heavy pressing, easy on the shoulders), and the straight-arm pullover stretches and pumps the lats and serratus. Keep the rests short — this block doubles as your conditioning, and the round-3 burnouts will have you breathing. That's your intensity and your heart rate today; no treadmill needed after two run-free days and a leg session.

blocks.title: CORE · DIRECT AB ISOLATION
blocks.meta: ~5 min · 16 kg · rectus-focused — a change from your recent anti-rotation core
blocks.format: 3 ROUNDS · minimal rest · slow and squeezed
blocks.workRest: Your last few core days were anti-rotation and loaded rotation — today matches the isolation theme and works the abs directly through flexion. Exhale hard and crunch the rib cage to the pelvis on every rep; make the muscle do it, not momentum.

items.name: Weighted KB Crunch
items.detail: 16 kg held on the chest · 15 · slow, exhale and curl the shoulders up, squeeze the abs at the top, control down. Loaded rectus work.

items.name: Lying Leg Raise
items.detail: bodyweight · 12–15 · low back pinned to the floor, legs straight, lower under control and stop just above the floor. Lower-ab focus.

items.name: Toe-Touch Crunch (V-reach)
items.detail: bodyweight · 15 · legs up, reach both hands toward your toes, crunch the upper abs and squeeze. Bail to a standard crunch if the hip flexors take over.

blocks.text: Direct ab isolation to match the day and to rotate off your recent anti-rotation/carry core work. Loaded crunch for the upper abs, leg raises for the lower, toe-touches to finish — all flexion, all squeeze. Five minutes, three rounds, done.

blocks.title: COOLDOWN
blocks.meta: ~3 min · flush the pump, open the front of the shoulders and the elbows you just torched
blocks.text: Walk or shake the arms out 30s to move blood. Then: doorway / floor pec stretch 30s/side · overhead triceps stretch 30s/side · cross-body rear-delt stretch 30s/side · wrist flexor + extensor stretch 20s each (you earned it after all that curl volume) · 5 slow nasal breaths. Report back: how the 21s felt, your near-failure RPE on the arm and delt work, and how much of a pump you got — that tells me whether to make isolation a recurring slot and how to load the delts next time. Legs get another day to recover before the next real leg session.

timer.emomUnit: No EMOM today — Block 1 = 4 supersets by feel (~45s rest, final round to failure). Block 2 = 3 giant-set rounds (~60s rest). Block 3 = 3 supersets, short ~40s rest, round 3 burnout. Use the STOPWATCH only to keep rests honest and short.
